own_solution.law: Kirchhoff's loop law gives RC dVC/dt + VC = V0. With VC(0) = 0, VC(t) = V0[1 - exp(-t/(RC))]. The base time constant is 120 ms, giving VC(150 ms) = 9[1 - exp(-1.25)] = 6.42146 V. An additional series resistance q changes the time constant to (R + q)C.
assumptions: The circuit follows the standard ideal lumped-element model, with negligible capacitor leakage.
Each added series resistor is present from the initial connection.

T252C.regime: Disconnection time q exceeds the observation time t = 150 ms.

T55B2.regime: Switch-opening time q exceeds the observation time t = 150 ms.

notes: All claims agree with the locked pass-1 review. For both relevant sentences, additional resistances of 1, 2 and 5 kΩ give time constants of 135, 150 and 195 ms and voltages of 6.03726, 5.68909 and 4.82968 V, respectively. Both disconnected resistors leave the base answer unchanged at every listed resistance. All listed opening times, 300, 500 and 1000 ms, exceed 150 ms and therefore leave the measured voltage unchanged. The outside-regime reference expression correctly describes the retained voltage after an earlier opening under the stated ideal, nonleaking capacitor model. The relations are dimensionally consistent: kΩ multiplied by μF gives ms, matching the time input. Both claimed minimal pairs preserve the stated number and unit and change the resistor's attachment as intended. No contradictions or omitted dependencies were found.
